open_issues: Nemotron-H official-precision gate fails at f9f78b5: cached row 22 is 0.998558 against its 0.998635 floor. It is attributed to the once-rounded Mamba-2 convolution SiLU, which decision (a) mandates and which matches F.silu at the op level. The floor rule (each path's worst official F16 row) needs a reviewed decision; nothing was tuned.

Awaiting the maintainer, decision (d): a library-level Gemma 3 F16 policy (default refusal plus opt-in, as a family-declared range hazard checked by a LoadOptions policy). For now only the gates refuse f16, and the library evaluates the overflowing graph.
Awaiting the maintainer, decision (d, Metal BF16): a Burn >= 0.22 upgrade (MSRV 1.95, backend-erased Tensor API). Burn 0.21 keeps the contextual refusal.
Awaiting the maintainer: a non-finite guard in generation, and a post-attention-add hook (v0.2).
Qwen2-7B in F16 stays uncalibrated. Burn's finite F16 logits rest on treating fully overflowed score rows as excluded. An envelope would need a rule change, for example SDPA-only graphs.
The opt-in eager attention graph (EagerFp32Softmax) exceeds the envelope in Qwen3-4B Flex/BF16 cached decode (1.106/0.157 against 1.054/0.100).
Gemma's Flex/BF16 cached decode step 13 sits at 94.5% of its bound and needs a targeted look.

The 0.5 self-consistency tolerance is still provisional for cached prefill, batched rows, and Gemma's long chunk ends; it needs official batched and chunked rows. The position-0-split envelope has not been derived. With the envelope tolerance, SmolLM-135M, SmolLM3-3B, Qwen2-7B, and Gemma long have no decisive greedy steps.

Burn Flex deviations to report upstream, now pinned by tests: the BF16 cast ignores the 3 low F32 bits; F16 matmul keeps F16 partial sums; tanh-GELU overflows for BF16 inputs >= 2^127. The other sites where Burn rounds scalars to the tensor dtype still need an audit.
Muse Q8 smoke peak variance is unexplained (31.89 GB this round; 31.87-45.68 GB earlier).
Not run: CUDA/ROCm, coverage qualification, the package gate, Gemma 3 1B/270m and Gemma 2 F16.
summary:
Decisions (a)–(c) are fully implemented in /Users/nover/repos/transformers-worktrees/tfm-half-followups2 (branch claude/tfm-half-followups2, head 8181605, 11 commits on 7bd057e). Decision (d) got only its least invasive variant: a gate-level Gemma F16 refusal, docs, and the Metal BF16 probe recorded; the library-level policy and the Burn upgrade are left for the maintainer.

The envelope rule's slacks come from the official graphs alone: BF16 1.5/1.3 (round 2 reproduced) and F16 1.7/1.7. Every Llama-family and Gemma F32 and Flex/BF16 gate passes, including all six October 17 failures, as do the F16-calibrated Metal/F16 gates. Qwen2-7B F16 is uncalibrated as decided. The advertised Qwen3.5-0.8B profile requalified: parity, benchmarks with a controlled rerun showing no regression, and memory. The larger checkpoints pass, and the Qwen3.8 Q8/Q4 conversions are byte-identical.

The one failing gate is Nemotron-H official-precision, traced by two controls to the once-rounded Mamba-2 SiLU. It is recorded as a finding and nothing was tuned. Source checks pass at 1816d73, and the final head passes the Python tests (560), the doc audit, and fmt. The evidence is in acceptance/measurements/half-precision-envelope-20261018.json and its campaign directory.
